solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nettle with grains male put in party dish

indicators.note: things put in something are placed inside it, so the first pieces go inside the last

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party
to nettle someone is to irritate them; anger is the irritation
sand is made of tiny grains
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A wild recipe: stinging nettles and grain with some male ingredient added to a party dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers and mash is the classic British dish of sausages (bangers) with mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages served with mashed potato is a traditional British pub meal, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Weapon traps set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nets are used to trap fish or birds

explanation.surface: A weapon has been rigged up with traps.
explanation.walkthrough: Traps looks like a verb belonging to the weapon, but it is a noun meaning snares. The Sten was a British sub-machine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten gun was a cheap submachine gun used by British forces, so it is a firearm.

clue.text: Half of capital raised for one

indicators.note: half of limits the operation to one portion of the word, so only that part is turned
in a down clue, raised means turned upwards, so the named portion is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway

explanation.surface: Half of a sum of money has been raised for one person or cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Only half of OSLO turns over: its first two letters OS flip to SO, and LO stays put. 'Capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo is performed by a single person, so it is a piece meant for one performer alone.

clue.text: Domestic gathering is large, but not here

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the first word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a domestic is a household servant such as a maid
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A large family gathering at home is going on, though someone is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like an adjective describing the gathering, but it is a noun for a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mislaid has been put somewhere and lost, so it is not to be found where you are.

clue.text: Straight-faced comic with vanishing act amazingly visionary

indicators.note: comic suggests something played for laughs and mixed up, signalling a reworking of letters
amazingly suggests the letters end up in a surprising new order
something vanishing disappears, so those letters are taken out of the fodder

parts.note: taken letter for letter
taken as written; these letters are the ones that vanish

explanation.surface: A deadpan comedian whose disappearing act is astonishingly prophetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, C and T from STRAIGHTFACED and the ten letters left rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone far-sighted plans well ahead and anticipates the future, much as a visionary does.

clue.text: Chamber below leg in car for drink

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a limo is a limousine, a large car

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means placed underneath, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: the on side is the leg side in cricket, so leg gives on
a cell is a small room or chamber

explanation.surface: A chamber beneath a leg room in a car, set aside for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, which is how leg can stand for on.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoncello is an Italian lemon liqueur, served as an after-dinner alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Write account with one engulfed by many approvals

parts.note: to author a work is to write it
an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a British tax-free savings account

indicators.note: something engulfed by another is swallowed up inside it

parts.note: tons is an informal word for a great many
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Writing up an account with someone surrounded by crowds of sign-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside TONS. An ISA is a British savings account, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorisations are formal permissions granted to do something, which is what approvals are.

clue.text: Under no circumstances con everyone

parts.note: con as in pros and cons means against, that is not for
the whole world means everybody

explanation.surface: Never, under any circumstances, swindle everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a verb meaning swindle, but it is the con of pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal meaning never, at any price or in any situation.

clue.text: Split parts of Minehead's oriental fare

indicators.note: the place name is to be broken into its component words, each translated separately

parts.note: the first part, mine: egg is old military slang for a mine or bomb
the second part, heads: noodle is slang for a head

explanation.surface: Somebody has broken up bits of something from Minehead, the Somerset seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a seaside town in Somerset; split it into mine and heads. Egg is slang for a mine or bomb, and noodle is slang for a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg noodles are a staple of Chinese and other East Asian cooking, so they are food from the Orient.

clue.text: Unavailable aged fable in which adept disappears

parts.note: aged forty is the same as of forty, as in a man of forty

indicators.note: something that disappears is removed, so the word for skilled is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
able means skilled or adept; these letters go

explanation.surface: An old fable can no longer be had, a story in which the skilled hero vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aged' looks like old, but it means of, as in a person of ninety.
explanation.definitionFit: When a dish is off the menu it cannot be ordered, so off means not available.

clue.text: Promise goatherd keeps

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the letters sit inside the word that follows

parts.note: the letters run consecutively inside this word

explanation.surface: A goatherd keeps a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeps a promise is a natural phrase, which hides the fact that keeps is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn vow or pledge, which is a formal kind of promise.

clue.text: Uncovered both wine and lodging here

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of a covering, so the outer letters of each word are removed

parts.note: the inner letters of this word
the inner letter of this word

explanation.surface: Wine and a bed both on offer, no cover charge, at a lodging place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both' tells you to strip two words: wine and the little word and. 'Lodging here' reads naturally as describing the place.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub offering rooms to travellers, a place where you lodge for the night.

clue.text: Presenting teacher afraid of forgetting article

parts.note: prof is short for professor, a university teacher

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so the article is dropped

parts.note: afraid of something is fearing it
a is the indefinite article; it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A nervous teacher, afraid of forgetting a piece of writing, is giving a presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an essay or object, but it is the grammatical word a.
explanation.definitionFit: Proffering means holding something out for someone to take, which is presenting or offering it.

clue.text: Fabrication engineers picked up drilled building material

parts.note: a fib is a small lie, a fabrication
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so what follows is said and not spelt

parts.note: a drilled hole has been bored

explanation.surface: Engineers fabricated a building material, picked it up and drilled holes in it.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a common crossword abbreviation. Bored and board sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibreboard is a sheet made from compressed wood fibres, used in construction for panels and partitions.

clue.text: English lark above duck in low flight path

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means on top, so one piece comes before the other

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: feeling low is feeling sad
a lark or a caper is a playful escapade
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An English skylark flies above a duck on a low flight path.
explanation.walkthrough: Lark and duck look like birds in flight but are a prank and a cricket score of nought. An escape road is a British term for a runoff lane on a hill or circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape road lets a runaway vehicle leave the main road safely, a route for flight in the sense of fleeing.

clue.text: Wheel crossing line causes obstruction

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the first word sits astride the next

parts.note: a cog is a toothed wheel
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A wheel crossing a railway line causes a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog is a blockage in a pipe or system, something that obstructs movement or flow.

clue.text: Vengeance by a revolutionary infiltrating group

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so these letters go within the group word

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves
taken as written

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the preceding words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolutionary infiltrates a group in pursuit of vengeance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a person, but it tells you to turn round the words by a.
explanation.definitionFit: Payback is retribution for a wrong done to you, which is revenge or vengeance.

clue.text: Sportsperson's healthiest around, scrubbing his bats

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order
bats means crazy, so the remaining letters are jumbled
scrubbing something means cancelling it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A cricketer, the fittest around, cleans his bats.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H, I and S from HEALTHIEST leaves seven letters to rearrange. Bats reads as cricket gear, but it means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person trained in sport and physical exercise, so a sportsperson.

clue.text: Cows just engaged in advances

indicators.note: engaged in means involved inside, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages
what is just is what is deserved, or due

explanation.surface: Cattle are simply being involved in the progress of farming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cows' looks like cattle, but it is a verb meaning intimidates. A sub is British slang for an advance payment on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission, which is to subdue them.

clue.text: This writer had regularly discarded clues not working

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, and I had contracts to I'd

indicators.note: regularly discarded means every other letter is thrown away, keeping the rest

parts.note: the second and fourth letters survive

explanation.surface: The setter had thrown out some clues that did not work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter speaking of themselves, so it gives I, and with had it becomes I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means unoccupied or inactive, so someone idle is doing no work.

clue.text: Throb with marks being tender once

parts.note: a heart or head that throbs pounds
to note something is to mark it; notes are marks

explanation.surface: A throbbing pain, with bruises, that used to be sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like sore, but it means legal tender, money. The Bank of England pound note was withdrawn in 1988 in favour of the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pound notes were paper money in Britain until replaced by coins, so they are former legal currency.

clue.text: Quickly go when your number's up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a PIN is your personal identification number

explanation.surface: A question: do you leave in a hurry when your time has come?
explanation.walkthrough: Your number's up is an idiom for death or being caught, which disguises the reversal instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip somewhere is British slang for to dash there briefly, as in nip to the shops.

clue.text: Competition buzzer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a contest such as a spelling ...
second meaning: an insect that hums as it flies

explanation.surface: A buzzer used in a quiz competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quiz show's buzzer; instead the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A spelling bee is a contest, and the insect makes a constant buzzing sound in flight.

clue.text: Better ring family man

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or better it
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Better to phone a man who has a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family man' reads as a devoted father, but the family is the Mafia: a capo is a crime boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo heads a group within a Mafia crime family, so he is a man of the family.

clue.text: Saving wine depleted after editor's abandoned working

parts.note: red is red wine

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the editor's letters are dropped

parts.note: something depleted has been emptied
ED is the abbreviation for editor; these letters go
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Saving wine that has run low after the editor abandoned work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' looks like keeping money, but it is a noun for rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Redemption is deliverance from sin or harm, which in religious language is salvation or saving.

clue.text: Some time scratching in silence

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so the next word's letters are removed

parts.note: a minute is a short period of time
taken as written; these letters are struck out

explanation.surface: For some time someone scratches away in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In silence' reads as one phrase, but in is the thing scratched out and silence alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To mute a sound or a person is to make them quiet, which is to silence them.

clue.text: Credit that's given when one's right

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the mark a teacher puts beside a correct answer

explanation.surface: Credit is what you get when you are proved right.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy on tick is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick is informal for credit, and a checkmark beside correct work is also called by this name.

clue.text: Repaired a cut lip, covering wound with one of medicinal preparations

indicators.note: covering means going around, so the rearranged letters wrap the next pieces
something repaired has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter
to wound is to harm
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A doctor fixed a cut lip, covering the wound with ointment from the medicine cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split in two, one letter in front and six behind. 'One' belongs to the wordplay, so the definition is the adjectival phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmaceutical is an adjective describing medicines and drugs, so it means relating to medicinal preparations.
